newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Market marked by bearish tone.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Market marked by bearish tone.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel markets continued to be weighed down by excess regional supplies as several deals were seen at lower levels, traders said.

Prompt gas oil traded at 20 cent below Wednesday's deal, chalking yet another year low. A European major sold the 150,000-barrel parcel to a Singapore trader at $24.30 per barrel for June 20-24 free-on-board basis.
The Singapore trader bought another cargo at $24.50 from a Mediterranean trader for the same timing. A third cargo was traded at $24.70 between a European major and a Japanese trader.
Traders said the overhang of prompt supplies were seen by the emergence of five sellers with eight cargoes, facing two buyers.
Also four 30,000-tonne cargoes were said to be distressed off China's southern coast, causing added concerns to the market.
Swaps gas oil also suffered under the current bearish climate as the inter-front months contango deepened.
June lost 20 cents to be last quoted at $24.45/$24.55, while July shed five cents to $24.60/24.70.
Jet fuel also fell with a 130,000-barrel cargo sold by a US trader to a a European major at $24.05 per barrel for June 20-24 lifting fob.
Nepal sold 30,000 tonnes of kerosene by tender to Vitol at $199.37 per tonne for July 1-10 delivery, cost-and-freight Indian east coast.
Nepal will decide next week to issue another kerosene import tender for July 21-31 delivery as well as diesel for August 11-20, August 21-31 and September 11-20 deliveries.
